title: The Prose Tristan
description: The Prose Tristan expanded the Tristan legend into a massive romance.
significance: The most popular version of the Tristan legend in the later Middle Ages.

title: The Roman de la Rose
description: Guillaume de Lorris began the Roman de la Rose.
significance: The most popular French poem of the Middle Ages, a vast allegory of courtly love.

title: Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda
description: Snorri Sturluson wrote the Prose Edda, preserving Norse mythology.
significance: The primary source for Norse mythology, without which much would have been lost.

title: The Poetic Edda
description: The Poetic Edda was compiled in Iceland.
significance: The most important source for Norse mythology and Germanic heroic poetry.

title: The Decameron
description: Giovanni Boccaccio completed the Decameron, a collection of 100 tales.
significance: A masterpiece of Italian prose, providing a vivid portrait of plague-stricken Florence.

title: Petrarch's Canzoniere
description: Petrarch completed the Canzoniere, a collection of 366 poems.
significance: The foundation of Renaissance lyric poetry and the model for the sonnet form.

title: Chaucer's Canterbury Tales
description: Geoffrey Chaucer wrote 'The Canterbury Tales' in Middle English.
significance: Established English as a literary language and provided a vivid portrait of medieval society.

title: Gutenberg Bible Printed
description: Johannes Gutenberg printed the first major book using movable type.
significance: Revolutionized the spread of knowledge and democratized literacy in Europe.

title: Construction of Angkor Wat Begins
description: King Suryavarman II began building Angkor Wat in Cambodia.
significance: The largest religious monument in the world, representing the peak of Khmer civilization.

title: University of Bologna Founded
description: The University of Bologna was founded, the oldest university in continuous operation.
significance: Established the model for universities worldwide and the tradition of academic freedom.

title: University of Oxford Founded
description: Teaching began at Oxford, which would become the oldest university in the English-speaking world.
significance: Became one of the world's most prestigious universities, shaping Western intellectual life.

title: University of Paris Founded
description: The University of Paris was established as a major center of theological learning.
significance: The leading theological university of medieval Europe, educating popes and reformers.

title: Al-Azhar University Founded
description: Al-Azhar University was founded in Cairo as a center of Islamic learning.
significance: The oldest degree-granting university in the world and the center of Sunni Islamic scholarship.

title: Construction of the Tower of London Begins
description: William the Conqueror began building the White Tower at the Tower of London.
significance: Symbol of Norman power and one of the most famous fortresses in history.

title: The Tale of Genji Written
description: Murasaki Shikibu completed 'The Tale of Genji', the world's first novel.
significance: The world's first novel, providing an unparalleled portrait of Heian-period Japanese court life.

title: Construction of Cologne Cathedral Begins
description: Construction began on the Cologne Cathedral in Germany.
significance: One of the largest Gothic cathedrals in Europe, taking over 600 years to complete.

title: Construction of Chartres Cathedral
description: Construction of the current Chartres Cathedral began after a fire destroyed the previous church.
significance: Considered the finest example of French Gothic architecture and stained glass.

title: Rumi Founds the Mevlevi Order
description: The followers of Rumi established the Mevlevi Order of whirling dervishes.
significance: One of the most influential Sufi orders, spreading Rumi's poetry and mystical teachings globally.

title: Alhambra Palace Completed
description: The Nasrid dynasty completed the Alhambra palace complex in Granada.
significance: The finest example of Moorish architecture and a UNESCO World Heritage site.

title: Construction of the Dome of the Rock
description: The Dome of the Rock was completed on the Temple Mount in Jerusalem.
significance: The oldest surviving Islamic monument and one of the most beautiful buildings in the world.

title: Great Zimbabwe Peak
description: The city of Great Zimbabwe reached its peak as a major trading center.
significance: The largest stone structure in pre-colonial sub-Saharan Africa, demonstrating advanced African civilization.

title: Construction of Borobudur Temple
description: The Borobudur Buddhist temple was completed in Java, Indonesia.
significance: The world's largest Buddhist temple and a masterpiece of Indonesian architecture.

title: Construction of the Leaning Tower of Pisa
description: Construction began on the freestanding bell tower of Pisa Cathedral.
significance: Famous for its unintended tilt, it became an iconic symbol of architectural miscalculation.

title: Notre Dame de Paris Completed
description: The Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris was completed after nearly 200 years of construction.
significance: The pinnacle of French Gothic architecture and one of the world's most famous cathedrals.

title: Dante Completes Divine Comedy
description: Dante Alighieri completed his epic poem 'The Divine Comedy'.
significance: Established the Tuscan dialect as the standard Italian language and defined medieval cosmology.

title: First Performance of Everyman
description: The morality play 'Everyman' was first performed in England.
significance: The most famous medieval morality play, exploring themes of death and salvation.

title: Hildegard of Bingen's Visions
description: Hildegard of Bingen began recording her mystical visions and compositions.
significance: A polymath who composed music, wrote medical texts, and founded a monastery.

title: Construction of the Great Mosque of Samarra
description: The Great Mosque of Samarra with its famous spiral minaret was completed in Iraq.
significance: The largest mosque of its time and an iconic example of Islamic architecture.

title: Construction of the Hagia Sophia
description: Emperor Justinian completed the Hagia Sophia in Constantinople.
significance: The greatest church in Christendom for nearly 1,000 years, a masterpiece of Byzantine architecture.

title: Construction of the Basilica of San Vitale
description: The Basilica of San Vitale in Ravenna was completed.
significance: The most important surviving example of early Christian Byzantine art and architecture.

title: Construction of the Church of San Lorenzo
description: Filippo Brunelleschi designed the Church of San Lorenzo in Florence.
significance: A masterpiece of Renaissance architecture, establishing the classical vocabulary of the new style.

title: Masaccio's Trinity
description: Masaccio painted the Trinity in Santa Maria Novella, Florence.
significance: The first painting to use perfect linear perspective, revolutionizing Western art.

title: Donatello's David
description: Donatello created the first free-standing nude statue since antiquity.
significance: Revived the classical nude and demonstrated the potential of bronze sculpture.

title: Botticelli's Birth of Venus
description: Sandro Botticelli painted the Birth of Venus.
significance: One of the most famous paintings in the world, embodying Renaissance humanism and neo-Platonism.

title: Leonardo's Last Supper
description: Leonardo da Vinci completed the Last Supper in Milan.
significance: One of the most famous paintings in the world, though it deteriorated rapidly due to Leonardo's experimental technique.

title: Michelangelo's David
description: Michelangelo completed his statue of David in Florence.
significance: The definitive symbol of Renaissance humanism and Florentine republicanism.

title: Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel Ceiling
description: Michelangelo completed the Sistine Chapel ceiling.
significance: One of the greatest achievements in the history of Western art.

title: Raphael's School of Athens
description: Raphael painted the School of Athens in the Vatican.
significance: The quintessential image of the Renaissance, bringing together the great philosophers of antiquity.

title: Titian's Assumption of the Virgin
description: Titian painted the Assumption of the Virgin for the Frari Basilica.
significance: Established Titian as the leading painter of the Venetian school.

title: Machiavelli's The Prince
description: Niccolo Machiavelli's The Prince was published posthumously.
significance: The most influential work of political philosophy, defining realpolitik for centuries.

title: Castiglione's The Courtier
description: Baldassare Castiglione published The Book of the Courtier.
significance: The definitive guide to Renaissance courtly behavior, influencing European manners for centuries.

title: Erasmus' In Praise of Folly
description: Desiderius Erasmus published In Praise of Folly.
significance: A satirical masterpiece that criticized the corruption of the Church and society.

title: Thomas More's Utopia
description: Thomas More published Utopia, describing an ideal society.
significance: Coined the word 'utopia' and established the genre of utopian literature.

title: Rabelais' Gargantua and Pantagruel
description: Francois Rabelais published the first book of Gargantua and Pantagruel.
significance: A comic masterpiece that satirized medieval learning and celebrated human vitality.

title: Montaigne's Essays
description: Michel de Montaigne published the first two books of his Essays.
significance: Invented the essay as a literary form and pioneered modern skepticism.

title: Cervantes' Don Quixote
description: Miguel de Cervantes published the first part of Don Quixote.
significance: The first modern novel and one of the greatest works of world literature.

title: Shakespeare's First Folio
description: The First Folio of Shakespeare's plays was published.
significance: Preserved 36 of Shakespeare's plays, 18 of which might otherwise have been lost.

title: Shakespeare's Hamlet
description: Shakespeare wrote Hamlet, his longest and most famous play.
significance: The most famous play in the English language and the definitive exploration of human consciousness.

title: Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet
description: Shakespeare wrote Romeo and Juliet.
significance: The most famous love story in the English language.

title: Shakespeare's Macbeth
description: Shakespeare wrote Macbeth.
significance: One of Shakespeare's darkest tragedies, exploring ambition and guilt.

title: Shakespeare's King Lear
description: Shakespeare wrote King Lear.
significance: Shakespeare's greatest tragedy, exploring the nature of power, family, and human suffering.

title: Shakespeare's Othello
description: Shakespeare wrote Othello.
significance: A powerful exploration of jealousy, race, and betrayal.

title: Shakespeare's The Tempest
description: Shakespeare wrote The Tempest, his final play.
significance: A meditation on art, power, and forgiveness, often read as Shakespeare's farewell to the stage.

title: Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
description: Shakespeare wrote A Midsummer Night's Dream.
significance: One of Shakespeare's most popular comedies, exploring love, magic, and dreams.

title: Shakespeare's Henry V
description: Shakespeare wrote Henry V.
significance: One of the greatest history plays, exploring the nature of kingship and war.

title: Shakespeare's Julius Caesar
description: Shakespeare wrote Julius Caesar.
significance: A powerful exploration of political assassination and its consequences.

title: Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra
description: Shakespeare wrote Antony and Cleopatra.
significance: A tragic romance exploring the conflict between love and duty.

title: Shakespeare's Twelfth Night
description: Shakespeare wrote Twelfth Night.
significance: One of Shakespeare's most perfect comedies, exploring gender, identity, and love.

title: Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice
description: Shakespeare wrote The Merchant of Venice.
significance: A controversial play exploring prejudice, justice, and mercy.

title: Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing
description: Shakespeare wrote Much Ado About Nothing.
significance: A brilliant comedy of wit and misunderstanding.

title: Shakespeare's As You Like It
description: Shakespeare wrote As You Like It.
significance: A pastoral comedy exploring love, identity, and the natural world.

title: Shakespeare's Richard III
description: Shakespeare wrote Richard III.
significance: One of the greatest villain roles in theatrical history.

title: Shakespeare's Henry IV
description: Shakespeare wrote Henry IV, Parts 1 and 2.
significance: Introduced Falstaff, one of Shakespeare's greatest comic creations.

title: Marlowe's Doctor Faustus
description: Christopher Marlowe wrote Doctor Faustus.
significance: The first great tragedy in English and the definitive treatment of the Faust legend.

title: Marlowe's Tamburlaine
description: Christopher Marlowe wrote Tamburlaine the Great.
significance: The first great English play in blank verse, establishing the form for Shakespeare.

title: Spenser's The Faerie Queene
description: Edmund Spenser published the first three books of The Faerie Queene.
significance: The greatest English epic poem, an allegory of virtue and the Tudor dynasty.

title: Sidney's Astrophil and Stella
description: Philip Sidney published Astrophil and Stella, the first English sonnet sequence.
significance: Established the sonnet sequence as a major English poetic genre.

title: Sidney's Defence of Poesy
description: Philip Sidney published The Defence of Poesy.
significance: The most important work of literary criticism in Elizabethan England.

title: Jonson's Volpone
description: Ben Jonson wrote Volpone.
significance: One of the greatest comedies in English, a satire of greed and hypocrisy.

title: Jonson's The Alchemist
description: Ben Jonson wrote The Alchemist.
significance: A brilliant comedy of London life, satirizing greed and gullibility.

title: Webster's The Duchess of Malfi
description: John Webster wrote The Duchess of Malfi.
significance: One of the greatest Jacobean tragedies, exploring corruption and revenge.

title: Ford's 'Tis Pity She's a Whore
description: John Ford wrote 'Tis Pity She's a Whore.
significance: A shocking tragedy of incest, pushing the boundaries of Jacobean drama.

title: Beaumont and Fletcher's The Maid's Tragedy
description: Beaumont and Fletcher wrote The Maid's Tragedy.
significance: One of the most popular plays of the Jacobean era.

title: Middleton's The Revenger's Tragedy
description: Thomas Middleton wrote The Revenger's Tragedy.
significance: A dark satire of the revenge tragedy genre.

title: Tourneur's The Atheist's Tragedy
description: Cyril Tourneur wrote The Atheist's Tragedy.
significance: A moralistic revenge tragedy contrasting with the amorality of The Revenger's Tragedy.

title: Massinger's A New Way to Pay Old Debts
description: Philip Massinger wrote A New Way to Pay Old Debts.
significance: One of the most popular plays of the Caroline era, satirizing greed.

title: Brome's The Antipodes
description: Richard Brome wrote The Antipodes.
significance: A satirical comedy exploring madness and social convention.

title: Milton's Paradise Lost
description: John Milton published Paradise Lost.
significance: The greatest epic poem in the English language, justifying the ways of God to man.

title: Milton's Areopagitica
description: John Milton published Areopagitica, a defense of free speech.
significance: The most eloquent defense of freedom of the press in the English language.

title: Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress
description: John Bunyan published The Pilgrim's Progress.
significance: The most widely read book in English after the Bible for over 200 years.

title: Pepys' Diary Begins
description: Samuel Pepys began his famous diary.
significance: The most important primary source for English social history of the Restoration.

title: Pepys' Diary Ends
description: Samuel Pepys ended his diary due to failing eyesight.
significance: The end of the most vivid and intimate portrait of 17th-century English life.

title: Dryden's Absalom and Achitophel
description: John Dryden published Absalom and Achitophel.
significance: The greatest political satire in English, using biblical allegory to attack the Whigs.

title: Dryden's All for Love
description: John Dryden wrote All for Love.
significance: The finest neoclassical tragedy in English, retelling the story of Antony and Cleopatra.

title: Congreve's The Way of the World
description: William Congreve wrote The Way of the World.
significance: The greatest Restoration comedy, a masterpiece of wit and social satire.

title: Wycherley's The Country Wife
description: William Wycherley wrote The Country Wife.
significance: A bawdy comedy of manners, notorious for its sexual frankness.

title: Etherege's The Man of Mode
description: George Etherege wrote The Man of Mode.
significance: The definitive portrait of the Restoration rake, modeled on the Earl of Rochester.

title: Behn's The Rover
description: Aphra Behn wrote The Rover.
significance: The most popular play by the first professional female writer in English.

title: Behn's Oroonoko
description: Aphra Behn published Oroonoko.
significance: The first English novel, a powerful anti-slavery narrative.

title: Swift's Gulliver's Travels
description: Jonathan Swift published Gulliver's Travels.
significance: A satirical masterpiece that attacked human pride and political corruption.

title: Swift's A Modest Proposal
description: Jonathan Swift published A Modest Proposal.
significance: The most famous satirical essay in the English language.

title: Defoe's Robinson Crusoe
description: Daniel Defoe published Robinson Crusoe.
significance: The first English novel and a foundational text of colonial literature.

title: Defoe's Moll Flanders
description: Daniel Defoe published Moll Flanders.
significance: A vivid portrait of a woman's life of crime and survival in 18th-century England.

title: Richardson's Pamela
description: Samuel Richardson published Pamela.
significance: The first modern English novel, sparking a revolution in fiction.

title: Richardson's Clarissa
description: Samuel Richardson published Clarissa.
significance: The longest novel in the English language and one of the greatest tragic novels.

title: Fielding's Tom Jones
description: Henry Fielding published Tom Jones.
significance: The most perfectly constructed novel in English, a comic epic in prose.

title: Fielding's Joseph Andrews
description: Henry Fielding published Joseph Andrews.
significance: A parody of Pamela that became a novel in its own right.

title: Sterne's Tristram Shandy
description: Laurence Sterne published the first two volumes of Tristram Shandy.
significance: The most experimental novel in English, anticipating modernist and postmodernist fiction.

title: Smollett's The Adventures of Roderick Random
description: Tobias Smollett published Roderick Random.
significance: A picaresque novel that established Smollett as a major novelist.

title: Goldsmith's The Vicar of Wakefield
description: Oliver Goldsmith published The Vicar of Wakefield.
significance: A sentimental novel that became one of the most popular books of the 18th century.

title: Walpole's The Castle of Otranto
description: Horace Walpole published The Castle of Otranto.
significance: The first Gothic novel, establishing a genre that would dominate Romantic literature.

title: Beckford's Vathek
description: William Beckford published Vathek.
significance: An Oriental tale that combined Gothic horror with philosophical depth.

title: Radcliffe's The Mysteries of Udolpho
description: Ann Radcliffe published The Mysteries of Udolpho.
significance: The most popular Gothic novel of the 1790s, establishing the conventions of the genre.

title: Lewis's The Monk
description: Matthew Lewis published The Monk.
significance: A shocking Gothic novel that scandalized readers with its blasphemy and eroticism.

title: Blake's Songs of Innocence
description: William Blake published Songs of Innocence.
significance: A collection of lyrical poems that revealed Blake's unique visionary imagination.

title: Blake's Songs of Experience
description: William Blake published Songs of Experience.
significance: The darker counterpart to Songs of Innocence, including 'The Tyger'.

title: Blake's The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
description: William Blake published The Marriage of Heaven and Hell.
significance: A prophetic book that inverted conventional morality and celebrated creative energy.

title: Burns' Poems Chiefly in the Scottish Dialect
description: Robert Burns published his first collection of poems.
significance: The most important Scottish poet since the Middle Ages, preserving Scots dialect.

title: Wordsworth and Coleridge's Lyrical Ballads
description: Wordsworth and Coleridge published Lyrical Ballads.
significance: The founding document of English Romanticism.

title: Wordsworth's Preface to Lyrical Ballads
description: Wordsworth added his famous Preface to the second edition of Lyrical Ballads.
significance: The most important manifesto of English Romantic poetry.

title: Coleridge's Kubla Khan
description: Samuel Taylor Coleridge published Kubla Khan.
significance: One of the most famous poems in English, written after an opium dream.

title: Coleridge's The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
description: Coleridge published The Rime of the Ancient Mariner in Lyrical Ballads.
significance: The greatest poem in Lyrical Ballads and a landmark of English Romanticism.

title: Byron's Childe Harold's Pilgrimage
description: Byron published the first two cantos of Childe Harold's Pilgrimage.
significance: Made Byron famous overnight and established the Byronic hero.

title: Byron's Don Juan
description: Byron published the first two cantos of Don Juan.
significance: The greatest satirical poem in English since Pope's Dunciad.

title: Shelley's Prometheus Unbound
description: Percy Bysshe Shelley published Prometheus Unbound.
significance: Shelley's greatest work, a lyrical drama of liberation and revolution.

title: Shelley's Ozymandias
description: Shelley published Ozymandias.
significance: One of the most famous sonnets in English, a meditation on the transience of power.

title: Keats' Ode to a Nightingale
description: John Keats wrote Ode to a Nightingale.
significance: One of the greatest odes in the English language, exploring art, mortality, and transcendence.

title: Keats' Ode on a Grecian Urn
description: John Keats wrote Ode on a Grecian Urn.
